title: La Obsidiana de Teotihuacán, VISTA STORIES
comment: obsidiana-teotihuacan (VISTA): taller de tallado de obsidiana frente a las pirámides de Teotihuacán, Estado de México. Caras comunes, no famosas; los cuatro se distinguen a simple vista.

chars.LAURO_ZEMPOALTECA: Mexican man from the State of Mexico, obsidian carver, 70 years old, thin, brown wrinkled skin, short grey hair, a grey mustache, round glasses on a cord, a beige work shirt with rolled sleeves, a dark canvas apron with stone dust, grey trousers, his hands empty.
chars.PALOMA_ZEMPOALTECA: Mexican woman, 29 years old, brown skin, long straight black hair loose, a white blouse under a dark-red cardigan, jeans, ankle boots, her hands empty.
chars.BRANDON_VILLASENOR: Mexican man, 33 years old, light skin, short bleached-blond hair, a light stubble, a tight black polo shirt, a gold watch, white trousers, white sneakers, his hands empty.
chars.DRA_IBARRA: Mexican museum director, 52 years old, elegant, brown skin, black hair in a neat low bun, black-rimmed glasses, a navy-blue tailored blazer over a white blouse, a silver necklace, black trousers, holding a leather folder.

locs.LOC_TALLEROBSIDIANA: Small obsidian carving workshop with an open front near the Pyramid of the Sun in Teotihuacán, State of Mexico, in the afternoon: wooden shelves with shiny black obsidian masks, figures and knives-free decorative pieces, a carving bench with a grinding wheel, a dusty yard with nopal cacti, the great stone pyramid in the distance, warm light, no readable text, no signs, no logos, no people.
